# Lead magnet — Los dos umbrales y el problema de la "Zona 2"

**Home doc for `zonas-de-entrenamiento.pdf`** — the guide sent to every contact-form prospect and every CoachMatch lead. Decisions and open questions live here; the technical build record goes to `ai-infrastructure-documentation.md`.

**Status, September 5, 2026: shipped in all three languages.** 8 pages each, ~156 KB each, generated by `automation/build-zones-guide-pdf.js` from `automation/zones-guide-content.js` and `data/zones.csv`.

| lang | file | build |
|---|---|---|
| ES | `site/assets/guias/zonas-de-entrenamiento.pdf` | `node automation/build-zones-guide-pdf.js es` |
| EN | `site/assets/guias/training-zones.pdf` | `… en` |
| PT | `site/assets/guias/zonas-de-treino.pdf` | `… pt` |

**The ES file keeps its original name and path**, so every already-sent email, the two n8n workflows, `site/members/guias/index.njk`, `site/blog/como-elegir-tu-plan-de-maraton.njk` and the `automation/Caddyfile` redirect keep working with **zero downstream edits**. EN and PT are new files with no legacy URL, so they need no redirect.

⚠️ ***Shipping the files is not shipping the languages.*** *Nothing yet sends the EN or PT file to anyone — see* **What the translation does not fix** *below. That gap existed before this rebuild and is now visible rather than hidden behind a Spanish-only guide.*

**Playwright is not currently installed in this repo** — `npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium` first. (The Aug 13 sessions-guide build had it; it is not in `package.json` and is gone from `node_modules`. Worth adding as a devDependency the next time either guide is rebuilt.)

**Sibling, not duplicate: `lead-magnet-sesiones-por-zona.md`.** That one explains *what to do* in each zone, per sport. This one explains *what the zones are* and how the competing systems line up. This is the upstream half of the funnel and it closes by pointing at that one.

---

## Why it was rebuilt

`open-loops.md` NEXT, Sept 3, 2026 — Iván: *"it's old, ugly, we are sending it when a prospect fills the form and I don't like it."* The audit that followed found the ugliness was the least of it.

**Six failures were found in the old PDF; four of them were content, not design.** They are recorded here because they are the reason the new file is shaped the way it is, and because the same mistakes are cheap to make again.

1. **🚨 It told the reader to minimise two of our own key sessions.** The old guide mapped 5-zone Z3 and Z4 into the 3-zone model's Zone 2 and labelled both *"genera mucha fatiga para la adaptación que ofrece · a minimizar"*. `site/_data/zoneCopy.json` calls Z3 **"Extensivo de umbral. Sesión clave"** and Z4 **"Intensivo de umbral. La otra sesión clave"**, and `methodology.md` §5 lists a weekly session above threshold as a non-negotiable. *A prospect read that guide, bought coaching, and got a plan contradicting it in week one.*
2. **The distribution was stated as pure 80/20.** `methodology.md` §5 is **80/15/5 or 70/25/5**, shifting pyramidal near the race. The middle is trained on purpose, 15–25% of the volume. Separately, even Seiler's own elite data carries 5–10% moderate work — the zero-percent version is the YouTube compression, not the source.
3. **It promised 7 zones and delivered a generic 5.** Zone X and Zone Y never appeared. Worse, the borrowed chart on the last page labelled *its* 7-zone row `Z0 · Z1 · Z2 · Z3 · Z4 · Z5a/b/c` — a different model entirely. A reader who finished that PDF and opened the calculator saw a table matching nothing they had just read.
4. **The bridging number was never given.** Everything this business publishes is anchored at **100% = LT2 = threshold**. That makes the mapping arithmetic. It was absent, which is precisely why the guide could not resolve the confusion it existed to resolve.
5. **Dated or overstated science:** FTP defined as "60 minutes" while the same document said TTE at FTP is 30–70 (we publish a whole article on that myth); *"está demostrado que el RPE se correlaciona directamente con el lactato"*; **three mutually contradicting RPE mappings in one file**; "umbral anaeróbico" as the primary name for LT2; lactate rise attributed to carbohydrate use as its cause; **MAF named as a synonym for Z1/Z2**, importing a max-HR model into a business that anchors nothing on max HR; and a worked example that called 100% FTP a Zone 4 effort.
6. **Production:** three raw `$\rightarrow$` LaTeX artifacts inside tables, a broken sentence on page 1, a broken word in a table cell, "Tria Performance" against the wordmark — and **a third-party infographic redistributed under the caption "Sin fuente declarada."** *That one is the reason not to reuse any asset from the old file: it shipped a copyrighted chart while stating in print that we did not know whose it was.*

---

## Standing decisions

**1 · Every number in the figures is computed from `data/zones.csv` at build time. No percentage is typed anywhere.**
This is the decision the whole rebuild turns on. The old PDF was a **fifth hand-typed copy** of the zone model, it had drifted, and nobody had checked it against the owner file since `zones.csv` was created on Aug 10, 2026. The builder derives the axis, every band, every tick and both threshold markers from the CSV. Segments that merge zones are declared as **lists of zone IDs** (`[["Y","4"], "20–60′"]`), never as ranges, so a band that moves in the CSV moves in the figure on the next build. *There is no path by which this file and the calculator can disagree.*

**2 · The two anchors, and how honest each one is.**
`LT2 = 100%` is arithmetic — the threshold *is* the anchor, and it is the Zone 3 ceiling. **`LT1 ≈ 90%` is an approximation**, and the guide says so on the page: LT1 lands roughly 85–95% of threshold depending on the athlete. It is drawn as the Zone 2 ceiling because that is where it falls for most athletes, and the copy calls it a band rather than a line. *Do not let a future edit quietly promote it to a fact — the caveat is what makes the rest credible.*

**3 · The 3-zone model's Zone 2 equals Zone X + Zone 3. That is the guide's central claim.**
It is exact given decision 2: LT1→LT2 is 90→100%, which is X (90–95) plus Zone 3 (95–100). Zone Y (100–102) sits on the threshold line itself.

**3a · No "black hole." Decision by Iván, September 5, 2026, and it overturns his own earlier framing.**
The old PDF — and, in one line, `lead-magnet-sesiones-por-zona.md` — called the band between LT1 and LT2 *el agujero negro* and told the reader to avoid it. **That is wrong on the merits, not just in tone: well prescribed, that band is marathon pace, half- and full-Ironman pace, and the tempo work that is a key weekly session in these plans.** The guide now describes the moderate domain neutrally and puts the real point where it belongs — *the franja intermedia is prescribed, not improvised*. The cost being warned about is unplanned drift into it on an easy day, never the zone itself. **Do not reintroduce the pejorative label in the EN or PT translation.**

**3b · Zone X and Zone Y are not ours. They come from `80/20 Running` (Matt Fitzgerald).**
*(Iván, September 5, 2026 — he is explicit that he is not the author of that system.)* The guide credits it by name on page 3. **Two repo docs asserted the opposite — `methodology.md` §4 and `zones-calculator-brief.md` §2 both said "house conventions, not standard" — and both were struck through with a dated note in the same session.** A third copy is customer-facing and still live: `lead-magnet-sesiones-por-zona.md` says *"Les dimos nombre propio"*, which is shipped in all three sessions-guide PDFs. That one is logged in `open-loops.md`, not silently edited, because fixing it means rebuilding three published files.

**4 · Three figures, all ours, all vector. No borrowed images, ever.**
Fig 1, the lactate curve (inline SVG). Fig 2, the stack — one axis, five rows: 3-zone, 7-zone, RPE, sustainable time, session name. Fig 3, the two "Zona 2" bands on the same axis. Together they replace the two scanned third-party charts *and* the two large tables from the old file. **The old guide's second image had no attributable source and must not be reused in any language.**

**5 · One RPE mapping in the document, and one only.** Fig 2 gives the numbers; the talk-test table on page 6 gives the feel. They are generated from the same zone IDs. *The old file's three conflicting mappings is the failure mode this replaces.*

**6 · Same filename, same path.** Overwrite in place. The old URL is linked from already-sent emails, `automation/contact-form-workflow.json`, `automation/coachmatch-email-nurture-2-3.json`, `site/members/guias/index.njk`, `site/blog/como-elegir-tu-plan-de-maraton.njk` and a permanent redirect in `automation/Caddyfile`. Renaming would mean editing all of them and still keeping a redirect. *Nothing downstream was touched.*

**6a · Register: explanatory, never anticipatory.** *(Iván, September 5, 2026.)* The first draft opened with *"Si leíste que hay que evitar la zona 2… para que no vuelvas a dudar"* and carried the same shape throughout — presuming what the reader already believes, then correcting it. **It reads as defensive.** The guide now states what things are and lets the reader place themselves: *"«Zona 2» no significa lo mismo en cada sistema"*, not *"si te dijeron X, en realidad es Y."* **Watch for this in translation** — the anticipatory construction is easy to reintroduce, and it is the single note Iván gave twice.

**6b · Neutral Latin-American Spanish, tuteo. No voseo.** *(Iván, September 5, 2026.)* The first ES build came out in rioplatense voseo — **26 forms**: `podés`, `tenés`, `sostenés`, `salís`, `sentís`, `terminás`, `elegís`, `cambiás`, `cancelás`, `querés`, `traés`, `entrenás`, `estimás`, `acabás`, `aguantás`, `contás`, `hablás`, plus the imperatives `bajá`, `mantené`, `Pedila`, `Escribinos`, `Elegí`, `Encontrá`, and one `para vos`. All converted.

**This was a regression against an existing house standard, not a new decision.** `automation/lead-magnet-content.js` — the shipped sessions guide, all three languages — is **pure tuteo with zero voseo forms**, and so is its home doc. Verified by a normalised sweep (`\w+[áéí]s`) over both files, not by eye.

*Check for it before every build.* One line catches it:

```
python3 -c "import re,io,unicodedata as u; t=u.normalize('NFC',io.open('automation/zones-guide-content.js',encoding='utf-8').read()); ok={'más','atrás','además','después','través','estrés','demás','inglés'}; print(sorted({w for w in re.findall(r'\b\w+[áéís]*[áéí]s?\b',t) if w.lower() not in ok and re.search(r'[áéí]s$',w)}) or 'clean')"
```

**6c · Decimal separator: period in ES and EN, comma in PT.** *(Iván, September 5, 2026 — "use 39.99".)* ES was `39,99` and is now `39.99`; EN was already `39.99`; **PT keeps `29,99` and `19,99`**, because the comma is the Brazilian convention and PT is a genuinely different price, not a formatting variant. *Note the sessions guide still shows `39,99` in Spanish — a one-character divergence between the two ES guides, logged rather than fixed here.*

**6d · The PT testimonials are translated from the original Spanish reviews.** They are real reviews from Chilean and Mexican athletes, rendered into Portuguese for a Portuguese-language document. **The shipped PT sessions guide still carries them in untranslated Spanish** — that reads as an oversight rather than a decision, and is worth fixing in `lead-magnet-content.js` on the next build of that file.

**7 · CTA order is All-Access first, coaching second, single plan third** — same call, same reasoning, as `lead-magnet-sesiones-por-zona.md`, Aug 13, 2026.

**8 · The CSS is duplicated from `build-lead-magnet-pdf.js`, not shared.** Deliberate for now: extracting a common stylesheet means editing the live sessions-guide builder, and design drift between two PDFs is a far cheaper failure than number drift. **This is the one known copy in the setup** and it is logged in `open-loops.md` rather than pretended away.

## Structure

| # | Page | Job |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cover | Zonestrip `1 2 X 3 Y 4 5`, X and Y highlighted — same device as the sessions guide |
| 2 | No hay un umbral. Hay dos. | Fig 1, then **three blocks in sequence: LT1 → entre LT1 y LT2 → LT2.** The middle block is load-bearing — it is what makes LT2 "exponential accumulation" rather than "the point where accumulation starts." Closes on lab → field → LT2 is the 100% |
| 3 | Múltiples sistemas, una fisiología | **Fig 2.** The page the guide exists for |
| 4 | "Zona 2" no significa lo mismo en cada sistema | Fig 3 + the two model descriptions + the translation + how to tell which one you are being given |
| 5 | Encuentra tu umbral | Test protocols straight from `methodology.md` §3, hygiene rules, calculator CTA |
| 6 | RPE y tiempo sostenible | One RPE mapping. TTE, and why Zone 4 exists |
| 7 | Cómo lo usamos | 80/15/5 → pyramidal; the middle band is prescribed not improvised; X as marathon pace; Y as the threshold band; bridge to the sessions guide; quiénes somos |
| 8 | CTA | Three offers, `page-break-inside:avoid` |

## What the translation does not fix — the delivery side

**The front end already carries the language. The workflows throw it away.** `site/_includes/partials/contact-form.njk` posts `language: "es" | "en" | "pt"` in its payload (line 80), and it has done so since the Eleventy cutover. `automation/contact-form-workflow.json` reads only `email, message, name, phone, sport` — the field is received and ignored.

**1 · Contact-form confirmation email — Spanish only, hardcoded.** *(The single biggest gap: this is the email every prospect gets.)* Node **`Send confirmation email`** has a fixed `subject` (*"Recibimos tu mensaje - Triaperformance"*) and a fixed `text` body carrying `https://triaperformance.com/guias/zonas-de-entrenamiento.pdf`. **An English or Portuguese prospect fills in an English or Portuguese form and receives a Spanish email with a Spanish PDF.** Spec for the fix lives in `contact-form-pipeline-runbook.md`; the work is n8n-UI only and is Iván's.

**2 · CoachMatch nurture — both sequences link the Spanish file.** `automation/coachmatch-email-nurture-2-3.json` **and** the Portuguese variant in `Claude outputs/CoachMatch-Email-Nurture-2-3-PT.json` both point at `/guias/zonas-de-entrenamiento.pdf`. The PT sequence was written in Portuguese and attaches a Spanish guide. **Now that `zonas-de-treino.pdf` exists this is a one-URL swap per sequence** — the cheapest of the three fixes and the one with a real audience already flowing through it.

**3 · `site/members/guias/index.njk` exists only in Spanish.** No `site/en/members/guias/` or `site/pt/members/guias/`. Separate and smaller; it is a gated page, not a funnel step.

**The pattern to copy already exists and is proven.** `zone-magnet-runbook.md` — the sessions-guide delivery via `/api/zone-workouts` — has been live in all three languages since August 14, 2026, keyed on the same `language` field. *Do not design a new mechanism; clone that one.*
